derivations.quote: With $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i),$ the [Two-point kernel C](phase-kernel.md) $C=aI+bX$ satisfies $H_0=b\,\mathsf SC\mathsf S,$ $C^2=X$ and $C^4=I$
Apply $\mathcal P_\Gamma^{-1},$ then $(C^{\eta_\xi})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ bits of slot $\xi,$ then $\mathcal P_\Gamma:$ one child on $f=e/m$ axes per residual vector, exactly $s$ in all.
Phases and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ are exact Gaussian dyadic, leaving $C^{\otimes D}.$
Their number is fixed, so the basis change and its inverse on $e$ axis chunks cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$
As $s/W\le m^\sigma,$ $\sigma<1,$ internal levels sum geometrically, leaves add $O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}),$ and $\log d$ pieces give $O(d^{\lambda'}).$
A depth-$\ell$ value lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell,$ since addition at most doubles modulus and halving adds a denominator bit.
Absolute row sums multiply under tensor products, so each row of $\mathcal H=H_0^{\otimes D}$ has absolute row sum one
Truncation toward zero cannot increase a component's absolute value and changes it by less than $2^{-p},$ so $Q_p$ keeps the disk, with $\|Q_p(\mathcal Hz)-\mathcal Hz\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$

relations.quote: $C^{\otimes e}$ is computed by the network of [Binary phase frames](phase-frames.md), with $W$ wires and $s$ smaller calls.
The layer obeys the recursion of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).
[Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md) XORs selected bits by cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a repair of exceptional addresses.
The layer is evaluated in [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md).

symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected address chunks, at most d.
symbols.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset, in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes ($D$ counts chunks, not the source group of the shear page).

symbols.name: selected axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group, e = mf.
symbols.quote: A group of $e=mf$ selected axes ($e$ counts axes, not digits of a chunk) has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

symbols.name: array
symbols.meaning: An array on which the diagonal operator acts.
symbols.quote: With $x_1,\dots,x_D$ the selected bits of an address $x,$ this gives $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D,$ where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ (not a suffix) by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

symbols.name: residual index
symbols.meaning: The index of a residual basis vector and its slot.
symbols.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_\xi C_{v_\xi}^{\eta_\xi},$ with residual basis vectors $v_\xi$ indexed by $\xi,$ $\eta_\xi=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

symbols.name: basis-change matrix
symbols.meaning: An invertible F_2 matrix whose first columns are the residual basis vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

symbols.name: address permutation
symbols.meaning: The address permutation sending x to Gamma x.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

symbols.name: standard basis vector
symbols.quote: so the edge change is $\mathcal P_\Gamma(\prod_\xi C_{\mathbf 1_\xi}^{\eta_\xi})\mathcal P_\Gamma^{-1},$ $\mathbf 1_\xi$ the $\xi$-th standard basis vector.

symbols.name: individual chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of leading chunks given individual C kernels, whose bits form the row index.
symbols.quote: So the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks get individual $C$ kernels, in $O(V\log d),$ and their bits form a row index of range at least $W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}.$

symbols.name: chain operation bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi(e)$ bound the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient ($E$ below is an operation bound, not a tensor factor).

symbols.name: invocation operation bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the operations in one invocation of the network.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi(e)$ bound the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient ($E$ below is an operation bound, not a tensor factor).

symbols.name: level factor
symbols.meaning: The sum s + psi, the factor by which the chain bound grows per level.

symbols.name: chain bound value
symbols.meaning: Any bound of at least one on a chain length.

symbols.name: exponent of m
symbols.meaning: The least j at least 1 with m^j at least Psi; an exponent, not a digit count.
symbols.quote: With $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ (an exponent of $m,$ not a digit count), $\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}\le\Psi^{\log_md+2}=\Psi^2d^{\log_m\Psi}\le\Psi^2d^\vartheta,$ so $\chi(e)\le8\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+1}.$

symbols.name: guard constant
symbols.meaning: The constant 128 m Psi^2 in the guard width Delta.
symbols.quote: The total is at most $8m\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+2}+18d<128m\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+3}\le\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil,$ with $C_0=128m\Psi^2,$ $C_1=\max\{20,\vartheta+3\}.$
